description: An encryption-key-policy artifact defines the cryptographic algorithms, key lengths, purposes, rotation schedules, and storage backends for every encryption key used by the application.

rules.description: The policy must declare a project name.
The keys array must contain at least one entry.
Each key must declare: id, algorithm, purpose, key_length_bits, rotation_days, and storage_backend.
Only NIST-approved algorithms are permitted. Deprecated algorithms (MD5, SHA-1, DES, 3DES, RC4, ECB modes, RSA-1024) are explicitly forbidden.
AES keys must be at least 128 bits; RSA keys at least 2048 bits; ECDSA/ECDH at least 256 bits; all keys at least 128 bits.
Each key must declare exactly one purpose. Compound purposes ('signing and encryption') or wildcards ('all') are forbidden.
The policy must include at least one key covering data-in-transit and one covering data-at-rest, unless tls_managed_externally: true.
No key may have a rotation interval exceeding 730 days. Purpose-specific limits apply: JWT/token keys ≤ 90 days, signing keys ≤ 365 days.
